arxiv-2107-06283.title: Analog Computing for Molecular Dynamics
arxiv-2107-06283.creator: Sven Köppel, Alexandra Krause, Bernd Ulmann
arxiv-2107-06283.description: Abstract Modern analog computers are ideally suited to solving large systems of ordinary differential equations at high speed with low energy consumtion and limited accuracy. In this article, we survey N N -body physics, applied to a simple water model inspired by force fields which are popular in molecular dynamics.

arxiv-2201-07340.title: Measuring High-Order Phonon Correlations in an Optomechanical Resonator
arxiv-2201-07340.creator: Y. S. S. Patil, J. Yu, S. Frazier, Y. Wang, K. Johnson, J. Fox, J. Reichel, J. G. E. Harris
arxiv-2201-07340.description: Abstract We use single photon detectors to probe the motional state of a superfluid 4 He resonator of mass ∼ 1 \sim 1 ng. The arrival times of Stokes and anti-Stokes photons (scattered by the resonator’s acoustic mode) are used to measure the resonator’s phonon coherences up to the fourth order.

arxiv-2212-02321.title: Dwarf AGNs from Variability for the Origins of Seeds (DAVOS): Optical Variability of Broad-line Dwarf AGNs from the Zwicky Transient Facility 2021 Dwarf AGNs from Variability for the Origins of Seeds (DAVOS): Optical Variability of Broad-line Dwarf AGNs from the Zwicky Transient Facility – A
arxiv-2212-02321.creator: Z. Franklin Wang, Colin J. Burke, Xin Liu, Yue Shen
arxiv-2212-02321.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Z. Franklin Wang, Colin J. Burke, Xin Liu, Yue Shen. We study the optical variability of a sample of candidate low-mass (dwarf ang Seyfert) active galactic nuclei (AGNs) using Zwicky Transient Facility g -band light curves. Our sample is compiled from broad-line AGNs in dwarf galaxies reported in the literature with single-epoch virial black hole (BH) masses in the range M BH ∼ 10 4 M_{\rm{BH}}\sim 10^{4} – 10 8 ​ M ⊙ 10^{8}\ M_{\odot} .

arxiv-2402-03420.title: MUSE-ALMA Haloes X: The stellar masses of gas-rich absorbing galaxies 2015 MUSE-ALMA Haloes X: The stellar masses of gas-rich absorbing galaxies – 4
arxiv-2402-03420.creator: Ramona Augustin, Céline Péroux, Arjun Karki, Varsha Kulkarni, Simon Weng, A. Hamanowicz, M. Hayes, J. C. Howk, G. G. Kacprzak, A. Klitsch, M. A. Zwaan, A. Fox, A. Biggs, A. Y. Fresco, S. Kassin, H. Kuntschner
arxiv-2402-03420.description: Abstract The physical processes by which gas is accreted onto galaxies, transformed into stars and then expelled from galaxies are of paramount importance to galaxy evolution studies. Observationally constraining each of these baryonic components in the same systems however, is challenging. Furthermore, simulations indicate that the stellar mass of galaxies is a key factor influencing CGM properties.

arxiv-2406-06629.title: A Survey of Features Used for Representing Black-box Single-objective Continuous Optimization
arxiv-2406-06629.creator: Gjorgjina Cenikj, Ana Nikolikj, Gašper Petelin, Niki van Stein, Carola Doerr, Tome Eftimov
arxiv-2406-06629.description: Abstract This survey examines key advancements in designing features to represent optimization problem instances, algorithm instances, and their interactions within the context of single-objective continuous black-box optimization. These features support machine learning tasks such as algorithm selection, algorithm configuration, and problem classification, and they are also used to evaluate the complementarity of benchmark problem sets.

arxiv-2407-21744.title: Assessing the Reliability Benefits of Energy Storage as a Transmission Asset
arxiv-2407-21744.creator: David Sehloff, Jonghwan Kwon, Mahdi Mehrtash, Todd Levin, Benjamin F. Hobbs
arxiv-2407-21744.description: Abstract Utilizing energy storage solutions to reduce the need for traditional transmission investments has been recognized by system planners and supported by federal policies in recent years. This work demonstrates the need for detailed reliability assessment for quantitative comparison of the reliability benefits of energy storage and traditional transmission investments.

arxiv-2412-02925.title: Effects of Landau quantization on neutrino emission and absorption
arxiv-2412-02925.creator: Mia Kumamoto, Catherine Welch
arxiv-2412-02925.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Mia Kumamoto, Catherine Welch. Some neutron stars known as magnetars possess very strong magnetic fields, with surface fields as large as 10 15 ​ G 10^{15}\,\mbox{G} and internal fields that are possibly stronger [ 1 ] . Recent observations of the radio pulsar GLEAM-X J1627 suggest it may have a surface field as strong as 10 16 ​ G 10^{16}\,\mbox{G} [ 2 ] .

arxiv-2502-08860.title: Brain in the Dark: Design Principles for Neuromimetic Inference under the Free Energy Principle
arxiv-2502-08860.creator: Mehran Hossein Zadeh Bazargani, Szymon Urbas, Karl Friston
arxiv-2502-08860.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Mehran Hossein Zadeh Bazargani, Szymon Urbas, Karl Friston. Deep learning has revolutionised artificial intelligence (AI) by enabling automatic feature extraction and function approximation from raw data. However, it faces challenges such as a lack of out-of-distribution generalisation, catastrophic forgetting and poor interpretability. In contrast, biological neural networks, such as those in the human brain, do not suffer from these issues, inspiring AI researchers to explore neuromimetic deep learning, which aims to replicate brain mechanisms within AI models.

arxiv-2505-12837.title: The Hidden Structure - Improving Legal Document Understanding Through Explicit Text Formatting
arxiv-2505-12837.creator: Christian Braun, Alexander Lilienbeck, Daniel Mentjukov
arxiv-2505-12837.description: Abstract The integration of Large Language Models (LLMs) into legal practice presents both transformative opportunities and significant risks, underscoring the need for rigorous benchmarking and a nuanced understanding of factors influencing their performance. Legal documents, particularly contracts, possess an inherent, semantically vital structure (e.g. sections, clauses) that is crucial for human comprehension but whose impact on LLM processing remains under-explored.

arxiv-2508-13053.title: A 15 Mpc rotating galaxy filament at redshift z = 0.032 z=0.032 2026 A 15 Mpc rotating galaxy filament at redshift z = 0.032 z=0.032 – References
arxiv-2508-13053.creator: Madalina N. Tudorache, S. L. Jung, M. J. Jarvis, I. Heywood, A. A. Ponomareva, A. Varasteanu, N. Maddox, T. Yasin, M. Glowacki
arxiv-2508-13053.description: Abstract Understanding the cold atomic hydrogen gas (H i ) within cosmic filaments has the potential to pin down the relationship between the low density gas in the cosmic web and how the galaxies that lie within it grow using this material.

arxiv-2509-20722.title: Parasitic actuation lag limits the minimum employable time headway in connected and autonomous vehicles
arxiv-2509-20722.creator: Guoqi Ma, Prabhakar R. Pagilla, and Swaroop Darbha
arxiv-2509-20722.description: Abstract . Adaptive and cooperative adaptive cruise control (ACC and CACC) and next generation CACC (CACC+) systems usually employ a constant time headway policy (CTHP) for platooning of connected and autonomous vehicles (CAVs). In ACC, the ego vehicle uses onboard sensors to measure the position and velocity of the predecessor vehicle to maintain a desired spacing.

arxiv-2511-22572.title: Formal Verification of Probabilistic Multi-Agent Systems for Ballistic Rocket Flight Using Probabilistic Alternating-Time Temporal Logic
arxiv-2511-22572.creator: Damian Kurpiewski, Jędrzej Michalczyk, Wojciech Jamroga, Jerzy Julian Michalski, Teofil Sidoruk
arxiv-2511-22572.description: Abstract This technical report presents a comprehensive formal verification approach for probabilistic agent systems modeling ballistic rocket flight trajectories using Probabilistic Alternating-Time Temporal Logic (PATL). We describe an innovative verification framework specifically designed for analyzing critical safety properties of ballistic rockets engineered to achieve microgravity conditions for scientific experimentation.

arxiv-2602-03776.title: DiffLOB: Diffusion Models for Counterfactual Generation in Limit Order Books
arxiv-2602-03776.creator: Zhuohan Wang, Carmine Ventre
arxiv-2602-03776.description: Abstract Modern generative models for limit order books (LOBs) can reproduce realistic market dynamics, but remain fundamentally passive: they either model what typically happens without accounting for hypothetical future market conditions, or they require interaction with another agent to explore alternative outcomes. This limits their usefulness for stress testing, scenario analysis, and decision-making.

arxiv-2602-04320.title: A Domain-Specific Curated Benchmark for Entity and Document-Level Relation Extraction
arxiv-2602-04320.creator: Marco Martinelli, Stefano Marchesin, Vanessa Bonato, Giorgio Maria Di Nunzio, Nicola Ferro, Ornella Irrera, Laura Menotti, Federica Vezzani, Gianmaria Silvello
arxiv-2602-04320.description: Abstract IE ( IE ), encompassing NER ( NER ), NEL ( NEL ), and RE ( RE ), is critical for transforming the rapidly growing volume of scientific publications into structured, actionable knowledge. This need is especially evident in fast-evolving biomedical fields such as the gut-brain axis, where research investigates complex interactions between the gut microbiota and brain-related disorders.

pmc-10531150.description: Sunburn is caused by prolonged exposure to ultraviolet (UV) rays from the sun, resulting in redness of the skin as well as tenderness, swelling, and blistering issues. During the healing process, it can cause peeling, irritation, and some long-term effects, including premature aging, pigmentation, and a high risk of skin cancer.

pmc-10555008.title: FRI070 The Urinary Extracellular Vesicles Small RNA Profile Of Obesity Displays Distinct Patterns By RNA Subclass
pmc-10555008.creator: Dughyun Choi, Sewon Kim, Soon Hyo Kwon
pmc-10555008.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Introduction: Urinary extracellular vesicles (EVs) small RNAs are thought to function as potential biomarkers for various physiological states and various diseases. Since urine contains a relatively small amount of microRNA compared to other biofluids, analyzing the distinct pattern of each subclass of small RNAs may provide additional information about gene expression. We attempted to analyze urinary EVs small RNAs by subclass in obesity before and after weight loss.

pmc-10577466.creator: Hyunsoo Chung

A study published in this issue, Yao et al,3 however, has shed new light on the role of the immune system in this disorder, offering valuable insights that may pave the way for more effective treatments.

pmc-10618222.title: Topology of turbulence within collisionless plasma reconnection
pmc-10618222.creator: Bogdan Hnat, Sandra Chapman, Nicholas Watkins
pmc-10618222.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). In near-collisionless plasmas, which are ubiquitous in astrophysics, entropy production relies on fully-nonlinear processes such as turbulence and reconnection, which lead to particle acceleration. Mechanisms for turbulent reconnection include multiple magnetic flux ropes interacting to generate thin current sheets which undergo reconnection, leading to mixing and magnetic merging and growth of coherent structures, unstable reconnection current layers that fragment and turbulent reconnection outflows. All of these processes act across, and encompass, multiple reconnection sites.

pmc-10632262.creator: Enric Tello, Vera Sacristán, José R. Olarieta, Claudio Cattaneo, Joan Marull, Manel Pons, Simone Gingrich, Fridolin Krausmann, Elena Galán, Inés Marco, Roc Padró, Gloria I. Guzmán, Manuel González de Molina, Geoff Cunfer, Andrew Watson, Joshua MacFadyen, Eva Fraňková, Eduardo Aguilera, Juan Infante-
pmc-10632262.description: Early energy analyses of agriculture revealed that behind higher labor and land productivity of industrial farming, there was a decrease in energy returns on energy (EROI) invested, in comparison to more traditional organic agricultural systems. Studies on recent trends show that efficiency gains in production and use of inputs have again somewhat improved energy returns.

pmc-10703751.title: Robotic-assisted total knee arthroplasty improves the rotational mismatch between femoral and tibial components, but not the forgotten joint score 12: a single-center retrospective cohort study

pmc-11351191.title: An Annotated Checklist of Invasive Species of the Phyla Arthropods and Chordates in Panama
pmc-11351191.creator: Digna Rodríguez-Gavilanes, Humberto A. Garcés Botacio, Rogemif Fuentes, Louise Rodriguez-Scott, Yostin Añino, Oscar G. López-Chong, Enrique Medianero
pmc-11351191.description: Simple SummaryInvasive species are considered a threat to the conservation of different environments. Annotating the numbers and species of these invasive organisms is critical to developing conservation strategies. This research gives background information on the types and possible origins of invasive species from the arthropod and chordate groups in Panama.

pmc-11443548.title: An exceptional phytoplankton bloom in the southeast Madagascar Sea driven by African dust deposition
pmc-11443548.creator: John A Gittings, Giorgio Dall’Olmo, Weiyi Tang, Joan Llort, Fatma Jebri, Eleni Livanou, Francesco Nencioli, Sofia Darmaraki, Iason Theodorou, Robert J W Brewin, Meric Srokosz, Nicolas Cassar, Dionysios E Raitsos, Stephen Palumbi
pmc-11443548.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Rising surface temperatures are projected to cause more frequent and intense droughts in the world's drylands. This can lead to land degradation, mobilization of soil particles, and an increase in dust aerosol emissions from arid and semi-arid regions. Dust aerosols are a key source of bio-essential nutrients, can be transported in the atmosphere over large distances, and ultimately deposited onto the ocean's surface, alleviating nutrient limitation and increasing oceanic primary productivity.

pmc-11652070.title: Anti Phospholipase A2 Receptor 1 Antibodies and Membranous Nephropathy Recurrence After Kidney Transplantation
pmc-11652070.creator: Marion Cremoni, Maxime Teisseyre, Olivier Thaunat, Céline Fernandez, Christine Payre, Alan Moutou, Hadi Zarif, Vesna Brglez, Laetitia Albano, Valérie Moal, Georges Mourad, Emmanuel Morelon, Bruno Hurault de Ligny, Philippe Zaoui, Eric Rondeau, Nacera Ouali, Pierre Ronco, Bruno Moulin, Laura Braun-Pa
pmc-11652070.description: IntroductionMembranous nephropathy can lead to end-stage kidney disease, for which kidney transplantation is the preferred therapy. However, the disease often relapses, which can impact allograft survival.MethodsWe conducted a prospective multicenter study in France involving 72 patients with membranous nephropathy who were awaiting and then underwent kidney transplantation. In addition, we established a retrospective validation cohort of 65 patients.

pmc-12644665.title: Design of minibinder proteins as universal antagonists against canine and human TNFα
pmc-12644665.creator: Jun Weng, Zhiyong Wu, Banbin Xing, Yang Hu, Xiaoyu Hu, Meng Mei, Jiaxin Xu, Mengqing Lu, Yibin Chen, Lin Wei, Ke Ming, Zhizheng Wang, Zhuang Li, Zigong Wei
pmc-12644665.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). In this study, we resolve the complex structure of canine TNFα (cTNFα) trimer bound to nanobody molecules at a resolution of 3.1 Å using cryo-electron microscopy. Structural comparison between cTNFα and human TNFα (hTNFα) reveals that the non-conserved residue Phe83 in cTNFα induces a conformational change in a nearby loop, which significantly reduces the binding affinity of cTNFα to nanobody TNF30.

pmc-12836802.title: Using causal effect estimation to evaluate occupational stress factors during a weekend on-call shift among general practitioners in training
pmc-12836802.creator: Géraldine Deberdt, Paloma Rabaey, Sam Van Damme, Laure-Ann Quenon, Peter Decat, Thomas Demeester
pmc-12836802.description: BackgroundIn recent years, our understanding of the various stress factors affecting the mental well-being of medical trainees during on-call work has grown. Although we have developed a general understanding, we still lack insight into the underlying interrelationships and causal effects of these factors, necessary to address and prioritize the mental health needs of young doctors.
